slides.title: An SLA is not a *design*.
slides.body:
Four nines on the contract.
One fiber path in the ground.

slides.title: Diverse on the invoice
slides.body:
Two carriers. One conduit. *One bridge.*
Adjacent in the dirt.

slides.title: Nobody asked the physical question
slides.body: The contract had already answered a *different one*.

slides.title: The credit doesn't run payroll
slides.body:
A fraction of one month's bill, eventually.
It compensates you for the outage — it was never built to *prevent* one.

slides.title: 1 — Where do the paths diverge?
slides.body:
On a *map*.
Not a logical diagram.

slides.title: 2 — Whose conduit is that?
slides.body: And who else is in it?

slides.title: 3 — What runs when primary is down?
slides.body: Everything — or the subset somebody chose *three years ago*?

slides.title: A design tells you whether it breaks.
slides.body:
An SLA tells you what you're owed when it breaks.

Follow *@mzsnetworks*
